title: Fast-path contributions and phased deprecation playbook
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: design contributors frequently open small, high-value changes (token tweaks, button variants, small chart updates) but the current governance requires a full RFC and multiple review rounds. This friction leads to stale fixes, inconsistent cross-team usage, and duplicate component variants.

Proposal: introduce a two-track intake and deprecation model: a 'fast-path' for low-risk, well-scoped contributions and a 'phased deprecation' framework for retiring components. Fast-path enables faster merges with guardrails (automated tests, pre-approved owners, lightweight review). Phased deprecation defines notice windows, migration helpers, and a gray-release pattern to preserve stability for products depending on older variants.

Scope: tokens (semantic token changes), atomic button states and sizes, table column utilities, chart color palettes and axis micro-adjustments. Not in scope: large API surface changes, breaking prop/behavior changes for core primitives, accessibility regressions without remediation plan.
acceptance_criteria: A documented fast-path intake checklist published to Confluence and linked from the DS contribution README
A template PR checklist (GitHub) that runs required automated checks and is enforceable by CI
A small pilot (3–5 PRs) using fast-path merged and results documented (time-to-merge and rollback incidence)
Phased deprecation policy published with timelines: notice window, grace period, and removal window
A migration-helper library (snippet examples) and a migration report template for PM/Eng owners
review_checklist: Is the change scoped to presentation tokens or non-breaking visual surface?
Has the contributor run the visual regression suite (per-PR) and attached baseline diffs?
Does the change include accessibility verification (contrast, aria updates) if relevant?
Is there a named owner for the component or token and is the owner auto-approved for fast-path?
Are API-level changes avoided? If unavoidable, escalate to RFC track
Are migration examples included when behavior differs (code snippets and Figma variants)?
Are metrics/telemetry hooks added for new behaviors where appropriate (usage counts, errors)?
Is there a rollback plan documented in PR description?
phased_deprecation_policy: Stage 0 – Informal: flag component as 'deprecated' in registry and solicit feedback (2 weeks)
Stage 1 – Notice: public deprecation notice in docs and changelog; owners produce migration helpers (30 days)
Stage 2 – Grace: allow continued usage but show console/dashboard warnings and run compatibility tests (90 days)
Stage 3 – Removal: component removed from main branch; tags preserved and maintenance branch available for exceptional fixes (180 days after notice)
migration_guidance: Provide a direct mapping table: old token -> new token with recommended transformation snippets
For button variants, include prop-level shim examples and deprecation-helper utilities (CSS variables, class aliases)
For tables: column-compatibility utilities and recommended column configuration migration steps
For charts: color-palette aliasing and axis label helpers to preserve layout while updating internals
Offer a migration-scorecard template for owners to measure customer risk and testing coverage
rollout_plan: Week 0: Publish draft playbook on Confluence and open PR to update CONTRIBUTING.md
Week 1–2: Run contributor workshop (design + eng) to walk through fast-path PR flow
Week 3–6: Pilot fast-path with 3 designated component owners; track time-to-merge and regressions
Week 7: Review pilot metrics, iterate on checklist, finalize playbook
Week 8: Announce stable policy, add automation (CI checks, PR template), and update docs and DS registry
decisions_log: Opted for two-track intake (fast-path vs RFC) to reduce churn while preserving safety
Fast-path will be limited to visual tokens and non-breaking surface changes — no API contract changes
Automated visual regression (per-PR snapshot) is a gating requirement for fast-path merges
Phased deprecation windows are prescriptive but owners can request exceptions via PM/Eval review
